/women-in-politics.title: My Framer Site
h3: In this project we gathered data, conducted research and subsequently developed information graphics to communicate insights on women's representation in Indian parliamentary politics
Has the feminist movement played a role in Indian politics?
Do women leaders build more inclusive policies?
What role does intersectionality play in Indian Politics
What are the hurdles that prominent women politicians have faced on their path to success?
How does India compare on the metric of women's representation on the global stage ?
We told our data story through three A 2 sized posters with each poster dedicated to a specific theme
POSTER I : History of women's representation in Lok Sabha
POSTER 2 : Women in Lok Sabha : A retrospective
POSTER 3 : Global comparison
Format: Print publicationSize : A2 foldable
It was decided that a printable format would work well for this project for care of sharing. A large A2 poster print was designed that could be folded into an A4 booklet.

This first poster sets the context for the project. It explores the timeline of the women's reservation bill, imagines an information portrait of a woman politician and maps out a time series analysis of women's representation in different constituencies.

while the first poster served to visualize the reservation debate this poster chronicles the careers lines and backgrounds of women in parliament. It begins with personal reading of women politician and an understanding of their career trajectories and moves to a quantitative narrative of women in parliament. On the reverse side of this poster is a visualization of all the 78 women in the 17th LS.

In this poster a global comparison of women's rights in the political space. contextualizes the Indian position, in terms of the milestones that have been achieved. It also establishes broader global patterns for women's representation in the political space.

/electoral-bonds.title: My Framer Site
h2: What else could have been done with the total amount of electoral bonds ?
h3: Most electoral bonds were donated to and encashed by ruling parties, whether at the central or state level, indicating their significant influence in electoral funding.
Half of all electoral bonds came from just 20 companies, potentially influencing policy decisions and political outcomes

By utilizing the unique ID numbers of bonds, a linkage was established between donor companies and political parties, revealing the correlation between companies contributing larger sums and major political parties.
Nearly 90% of purchased bonds were in denominations of 1 crore, suggesting that larger corporations acquired multiple bonds of this value.
Although bonds were acquired from diverse SBI branches, a significant majority were encashed in the central capital, indicating a connection between the received bonds and the ruling party.

The majority of companies purchased a limited number of bonds and donated them to one or two political parties. However, companies acquiring larger bond sums tended to donate to a wider array of parties.

The bulk of listed companies directed their electoral bond donations towards larger political parties. This trend underscores the inclination of corporate entities to align themselves with major political players, potentially seeking to secure favorable policies or relationships with parties holding significant sway in the political arena.

The predominant trend observed in the encashment of bonds by political parties occurred either during or in the month preceding major state elections. By timing their bond encashments strategically around significant state elections, parties may seek to capitalize on heightened political engagement and public attention to maximize their electoral prospects.
Certain companies have purchased electoral bonds exceeding their net profits, indicating the potential existence of shell companies or the utilization of illegal sources of unregistered income.
